dietEvidence.body: The enlarged, procumbent anterior teeth suggest specialised feeding, but no gut contents are known. The diet is unresolved.

sizeNote: Length and mass are estimates from incomplete material, not measurements of a whole animal.
tagline: A very small maniraptoran with four long ribbon-like tail feathers and a short, deep skull. The tail feathers are preserved; their display function is inferred.
summary: A very small maniraptoran with four long ribbon-like tail feathers and a short, deep skull. The tail feathers are preserved; their display function is inferred.

discovery.body: Named by Zhang and colleagues in 2008. The holotype, IVPP V15471, is a nearly complete skeleton on part and counterpart slabs from Daohugou, Ningcheng County, Inner Mongolia, with four elongate ribbon-like tail feathers. The species is known from this single individual.

fossilEvidence.title: Preserved material
fossilEvidence.body: The holotype, IVPP V15471, is a nearly complete skeleton on part and counterpart slabs, with four elongate ribbon-like tail feathers. The skull is known.

fossilEvidence.title: Stratigraphic and geographic occurrence
fossilEvidence.body: The Daohugou beds, Ningcheng County, Inner Mongolia, record the species in the Middle–Late Jurassic. The numeric range used here is ≈168–152 Ma; the age of the beds is contested.

anatomy.title: Preserved anatomy
anatomy.body: The tail bears four elongate ribbon-like feathers; the forelimbs are slender and the skull is short and deep with enlarged anterior teeth. The feather arrangement is preserved, but its display function is inferred.

behaviour.body: The tail feathers are plausibly display structures, but no behaviour is preserved. The animal is interpreted as non-volant because it lacks flight feathers; that is an inference from one specimen, not a direct observation.

reconstruction.body: A licensed life reconstruction is assigned to this record and credited in Sources and credits. The species is known from a single nearly complete skeleton with feather impressions. The reconstruction is an artist's interpretation of appearance, not a direct observation from the fossil record; preserved integument, where present, is described in the anatomy section, and the soft-tissue outline is otherwise inferred.

confidenceNote: The single holotype preserves four ribbon-like tail feathers and a simple body covering, but no pennaceous flight feathers. The age of the Daohugou beds is contested, and display and diet are inferred rather than observed.
